utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Madam Registrar, would you please call the case.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: This is Case Number IT-98-29-T, the Prosecutor versus Stanislav Galic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Madam Registrar. I was informed that the voice distortion is now functioning again, so we could resume the examination of Witness AH. Mr. Usher, could you please escort the witness into the courtroom. And Mr. Ierace, yes, please proceed. I made an observation yesterday as far as dates are concerned. It's not that important. If it's a mistake, fine. If it's really of some relevance, of course you are perfectly free to pay more attention to it. But if not...

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Mr. President, I won't pursue that. There are two other questions I seek to ask before I formally complete examination-in-chief. May I also inquire what channel the English translation is on? I tried 4, and I heard French.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Good morning, Ms. AH. May I remind you that you're still bound by the solemn declaration you made yesterday. I indicated yesterday to you that you would be examined by counsel for the Defence, but there are still a few questions remaining. So Mr. Ierace, please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Good morning, Madam. What time of day was it when your brother was shot?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AH [Resumed]
utterances.text: In the afternoon.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: What was the weather like at that time?

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Microphone, please.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, it was clear.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Mr. President, that completes examination-in-chief.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Ierace. So now the moment has come that you'll be examined by counsel for the Defence. Ms. Pilipovic, it's you who is going to cross-examine the witness?

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good morning.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Witness AH, good morning.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Good morning.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Witness, yesterday you said that between 1992 and 1994, you and your family - your brother and your mother - I didn't quite get that - that you were not living in Sarajevo. I don't know whether your father was also away.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AH [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, no, no. My mother was in Sarajevo. Only my brother and I were absent.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Can you tell us, you and your brother, therefore, lived outside Sarajevo.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AH [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: And when did you return to Sarajevo? Was it July 1994?

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: And whilst you were outside Sarajevo, did you come to Sarajevo now and then?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AH [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, of course not.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Did you attend school during that time?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AH [Resumed]
utterances.text: My brother did and I did not.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: You said that on the 22nd of July, 1994, with your mother and brother you had gone to visit your aunt, and then you stopped by a shop window on Miljenka Cvitkovica Street; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it is.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Can you tell us the number?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Let me see. No, I can't tell you. No, I can't tell you the number. I'm not even sure whether that street is still called that. I really do not know.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Witness, when you started for your walk, or rather, when you were on your way to visit your aunt that day, can you tell us if there was any fighting in the city?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AH [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, or we wouldn't have left the house.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: And do you have any knowledge whether during that period of time there was a ceasefire signed in Sarajevo?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AH [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is another thing I can't say with certainty, but my brother and I had returned to Sarajevo only about a month before that, and we entered the city using blue roads. Those were the roads that one could take to get into the city. And they were open even at the time when my

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: -- and then your brother said that he was wounded. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I'd also add that I saw a hole in the glass.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: You saw a hole in the glass.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Ms. Pilipovic, the interpreter did not interpret at least one word you said. That was the name of the brother. It will be redacted, but would you keep in mind that you are not supposed to mention that name. Yes. Please proceed. Just for your explanation, if someone, even if it would be yourself, mentions the name of your brother, because of the protective measures, we'll -- we'll correct both the transcript of this hearing and also the tapes. So don't worry about it. We'll take care that the protective measures are effective. Yes. Please proceed, Ms. Pilipovic.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Witness, you've just told us that you had seen a hole where the glass had been hit. Did I understand you correctly?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, you did.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: -- and where were -- was your brother?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Ms. Pilipovic, of course I didn't listen to the B/C/S channel, but it happened again. Yes. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Can you tell us where you and your mother and your brother were standing?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AH [Resumed]
utterances.text: We were standing one next to the other. But I cannot exactly -- whether it was first my mother, then my brother, then I or how, I just don't remember that, but we were all standing in front of that shop window.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: How far from the three of you were the children that you said were present there?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Children?

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. Were there any children nearby?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AH [Resumed]
utterances.text: I really do not remember right now. I cannot remember how many people were there.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: In relation to the shop window, can you tell us in what position were you, in what position was your mother, and what was the position of your brother? Do you remember that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AH [Resumed]
utterances.text: At that moment, as a matter of fact, as we -- when we set off, he was riding a bicycle. But then when we halted in front of the shop, he got off the bicycle. But I think he had his side to the shop, not facing the shop. But again, I'm not quite sure.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: So you are telling us that yet your brother was not watching the shop window?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, he was standing with us in front of it; but whether he was really facing that or facing me or my mother, I really don't know.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Can you tell us, if you can cast your memory back to that shop window in front of which you were standing, where was the hole? Where was the hole in that window? Was it there or somewhere else?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AH [Resumed]
utterances.text: There, of course. It was to the left.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Can you tell us how high was it?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AH [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I really don't know that.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Are you telling us that that shot which you say you did not hear and that all that you heard was the glass breaking down, can you tell us where was the bullet?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AH [Resumed]
utterances.text: What do you mean, "where was the bullet"? I don't understand.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Where was the bullet?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I suppose it ended up in the shop. I saw this hole in the window, so presumably it landed in the shop. But I didn't see the bullet as a bullet.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: You told us that you went back to the site.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AH [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is right.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Can you then tell us whether at the time when you went back to the site, whether there were members of the police there? And do you have any knowledge if that part of that site where you had been was taken photographs of?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AH [Resumed]
utterances.text: When we returned there to that shop in front of which my brother was wounded, there is a coffee bar there. And two men came out of that coffee bar, those who helped us. And the bicycle had stayed in that coffee bar so that when we returned from the hospital, we went with those men into the coffee bar to get the bicycle. But there were no military there, no, inside that coffee bar. No, there weren't.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Can you tell us how old were the men who helped you?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, they could have been 40ish, in their 40s.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Can you tell us what they were wearing?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Civilian.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Perhaps you didn't quite understand me. My question to you was when you returned to get the bicycle, whether you found there or whether you heard that there had been the police there, taking photographs of the place of the site of the incident?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AH [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Witness, if I now show you photographs of the shop, would you be able to point at the place where there was a hole in the glass?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, more or less, yes, approximately.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, the Defence has photographs, 2792. These are photographs that we used when -- in the examination of the Witness Mirsad Kucanin.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. I'm afraid, Ms. Pilipovic, we have to wait until the registrar returns. Madam Registrar, could you please find Exhibit P2792. No, that is an exhibit that has been used before, during the testimony of Mr. Kucanin.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Whilst that is being located, I note that there are references to the name of Witness AG in the text accompanying those photographs which have not been redacted. I presume that --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Well, let's take care that if the photos are shown, that these names, if any text is visible, that it should be covered by one of our yellow stickers.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, the Defence has it, and we've covered this so that the Registry doesn't have to bother. We have covered this, and we can put it on the ELMO and the witness can look at it. We've covered it so this can be put on the ELMO, and the witness can then tell us that is the shop, of course, if my learned friend has no objections.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Assuming it is the same set, we could use it meanwhile until the Registry has found it. Mr. Usher, could you please assist Ms. Pilipovic. That saves us time in covering the...

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Witness, do you see that photograph? Do you have a photograph in front of you? And in the right -- bottom right-hand corner, just below this grid, it says number 1?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Can you confirm for us that this is the shop -- the window of the shop in front of which you were standing at the time; you, your mother, and your brother?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we zoom in this part with these bars, with this metal grate. Just can you bring the photograph down a little bit. Yes, good. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Witness, on this photograph, can you identify the place where the hole in the glass was? Can it be seen here?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AH [Resumed]
utterances.text: On this photograph, I see -- I do not see any hole. But as I said, it was on the left-hand side of the shop window. How high from the ground, I really don't know, but I saw it.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Is it this left-hand corner of the photograph? Higher up? Do you think it is higher up?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AH [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's right. Yes, on the left side, on the left side of this Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. photograph.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: So you are confirming to us that that hole cannot be seen on this photograph and that it is not in this part of the photograph that you have in front of you?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AH [Resumed]
utterances.text: I do not see a hole here, but I repeat once again that I did see it.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Can you tell us, at that moment, did you hear the shot?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AH [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I didn't.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: So you are confirming for us that you did not hear a single shot?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AH [Resumed]
utterances.text: At that moment, no, only the burst and the hole in the glass.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Witness, on this photograph, in this part which you have on the screen now, you are confirming now that all three of you were in this part that we see here in front of the shop window?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, of course.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Can you confirm that at that moment, as you were standing in front of that shop window, that there were these -- this metal grate was over the window?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AH [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't remember it being there. I really don't.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: So you cannot confirm for us that at the moment when the incident happened, you cannot confirm that the site, that the scene looks exactly as it is shown in this photograph?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, it is the exact site, but whether there was this metal grate here or not, I really don't remember. It was in 1994.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Witness, do you have any knowledge if your mother made a statement related to this incident to the law enforcement authorities of the Republic of Bosnia-Herzegovina?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Can you confirm for us that it was on the 1st of March, 1995?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AH [Resumed]
utterances.text: I wouldn't know the exact date. I really wouldn't.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, the Defence intends to show the witness the statement which her mother signed, but before that, we'd like the witness to look at a statement which is in B/C/S, but we also have the English translation. We want the witness to confirm whether it is her mother's signature on the statement. And then the Defence will show, will draw attention to a part of the mother's statement in relation to the event, to the incident which happened in front of this shop. This is the Prosecution document which is registered, and we have two ERN numbers, 00360886, and that is the statement made on the 1st of March, 1995, by the mother. And I also have some copies for my learned friends. Perhaps they could look at them, and if there are no objections, I'd like to show it to the witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I hear no objection, so you're --

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Mr. President, if my friend does have a copy, I'd be grateful for the copy.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. I think it was offered to you. Would you please take care. I don't know whether you've checked whether there are any names mentioned in the document, so perhaps you should be careful before putting anything on the ELMO. But the question about the signature, of course, can be --

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, there is no need to put this document on the ELMO, because we have a sufficient number of copies, and we only wanted the witness to confirm to us that this is her mother's signature on this statement.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Usher, could you please give the copies to --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, it is.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ... Ms. Pilipovic, is there any need that the document will remain with the witness or -- well, please proceed. We always can take it back to you later.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I don't think there's any need for it.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Witness, on this document that is in front of you, do you recognise your mother's signature?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Are you confirming that the statement signed by your mother, that there is the date the 1st of March, 1995, in the corner?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's right.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: And next to the signature which your mother signed, do you also see the 11th of November, 1995?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AH [Resumed]
utterances.text: I do.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Witness, you said today -- you told us today that you, your brother and your mother were standing next to one another at the moment when you heard the glass going burst. In the first statement that your mother gave in 1995, can you confirm that her memory in relation to this incident was better then than -- than your testimony in relation to this incident today?

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Mr. President, I object to that question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. The -- Ms. Pilipovic, the witness cannot answer the question whether the recollection of her mother was better at a certain moment or not. So the objection is sustained.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Witness, if I show you a part of your mother's statement which she made on the 1st of March, 1995, and confirmed it on the 11th of November, 1995 -- I will read the third line from the statement, that is, the fourth line, in the middle: "And whilst I and my daughter were looking at the window shop at a distance of three or four metres, there was my son standing, too, with his bicycle. We suddenly heard just the burst of the glass, and after that, he wailed," meaning your brother, "and children who were there started to run towards a nearby building." Witness, can you confirm for us whether your brother was three to four metres away from you and your mother or are -- or will you confirm what you told us today?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AH [Resumed]
utterances.text: I cannot confirm it. All I can say is that all three of us were standing in front of the shop window. How far, how far, half a metre, a metre, two metres, I really don't know, but we were all in front of that shop window.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Does that mean that you do not remember exactly how far you were standing one from another in relation to the shop window?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, but the distances were not big.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Do you allow it that you were standing at some distance one from another but you don't know how much?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AH [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know how much. I really don't.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Can you confirm for us, how were you standing in relation to one another, the line, the order in which you were standing there?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AH [Resumed]
utterances.text: I really don't remember.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Can you answer whether, after you returned to get the bicycle, did you see whether the glass panes on the coffee bar were also shattered, and did any one of those present tell you that a bullet had hit the coffee bar?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AH [Resumed]
utterances.text: When we returned to the scene, I did not come back to the shop. We entered the coffee bar through the rear door, and we came out of it also. But when we got there, a man - and I do not know whether he was a patron or whether he worked there - pointed to us a hole in the wall. That is it. And we also left through the rear door.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: He pointed to a hole in the wall where, in the coffee bar?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Did he tell you, then, when was it that this coffee bar was fired at? And since when did this hole date?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AH [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was after my brother's wounding. Whether it was ten minutes, half an hour or how much later, I really don't know because we had left for the hospital.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Can you describe the car which took you to the hospital? Do you know the make?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AH [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I really don't. I mean, we first went to the emergency unit, which was nearby, and then we went on to the hospital in an ambulance car. And what the make of the car was, I really don't know.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Can you -- do you have any knowledge if your mother reported the incident to the police? Did she -- was she interviewed that day by the police in relation to the incident?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AH [Resumed]
utterances.text: I really don't know.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Did you personally, apart from the statement to the investigator, did you make any statements to anyone else?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AH [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I didn't.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: What about your brother?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AH [Resumed]
utterances.text: He did. But when was that, I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: The car in which you rode to the hospital, can you tell us whether it had any markings or was it just a plain passenger car?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AH [Resumed]
utterances.text: A plain passenger car.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Did you -- as you stood there in front of the shop window when you heard the glass breaking, did you personally make an assessment as to the direction from which the bullet had come?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, you know, I really know nothing about weaponry, so I do not think myself competent to answer such a question.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, the Defence has no further questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you very much, Ms. Pilipovic. Mr. Ierace, any need to re-examine the witness?

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: No questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Ms. AH, I'll first ask whether any of my colleagues have any questions. I have one small question to you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Ms. Pilipovic asked you whether the car in which you rode to the hospital, whether this was just a plain passenger car, and you said it was a plain passenger car. Earlier, you testified that you were brought to an emergency first in a car, and then in an ambulance to the hospital. When you said that it was a plain passenger car, did you mean the car which brought you to the emergency or, later on, the ambulance that took you to the hospital?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AH [Resumed]
utterances.text: The one that took us to the emergency department. But these two men who came to our aid stayed with us in the hospital, and then we returned with them to the coffee bar to pick up the bicycle.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, but you were transported from the emergency to the hospital in an ambulance?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Ms. AH, this concludes your testimony in this Court. It has been a long voyage for you to come here, but you'll understand that it's very important that this Court hears the answers given to the questions put to you by both parties and by the Bench itself. So therefore, I thank you very much for having come to The Hague, and I wish you a safe journey home again. Mr. Usher --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: -- could you please lead the witness out of the courtroom.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Madam Registrar, could you please guide us through the documents.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Exhibit P3676, name sheet, under seal. Exhibit P3269, set of four photographs, under seal. Exhibit D80, the witness statement, under seal.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: These documents are admitted in evidence. Mr. Ierace.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Mr. President, before I call the next witness --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: -- which is AG, being the brother of the last witness, I observed that there are a number of exhibits on the list of potential exhibits in respect of this witness. I propose to tender none of them and, indeed, only to rely upon one which is already in evidence and not even show that to the witness. That particular document is P2794, which was tendered through Dr. Nakas from the State Hospital. I inform the Chamber of my intentions at this stage so as to assist the Trial Chamber and the Defence in understanding what will transpire. The reason I don't seek to tender the documents is that, when one looks at them, they are fairly technical. The only one that gives any overview in relation to these injuries is the document which is already in evidence before Dr. Nakas. Basically, I don't think that the other documents will be of any practical assistance to the Trial Chamber. But because my friends have them, of course they can cross-examine on them. Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you for your explanation, Mr. Ierace. Since one of the protective measures granted in respect of the witness is voice distortion, I wonder whether we should have a break first. I think it's -- we need to prepare the voice distortion, which is adapted to the voice of the witness. We could do two things, either to have the long break now and then split up the remaining time in two and have the shorter break afterwards; we also could have a very short break and perhaps continue in -- five minutes would be enough?

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Mr. President, it may assist you in making that decision to know that we are moving this week much faster than we anticipated, and it may be that we run out of witnesses before tomorrow afternoon. I think we only have two remaining witnesses, including this one.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: So you're asking us to slow down a bit.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: I'm saying that we can take a longer break than we otherwise would, but I don't propose to slow down, no.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Ierace, experience has learned me that what time is available is best assessed at the end of the examination of witnesses and not at the beginning. I suggest that we have a break for ten minutes. --- Break taken at 10.06 a.m.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I take it that the voice distortion is now prepared and functioning. Mr. Ierace, would you please call your next witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: I call Witness AG.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Usher, would you please lead the witness into the courtroom.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Good morning. Can you hear me in a language you understand?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It's not quite loud enough.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could you speak a bit louder perhaps.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I can't hear too well, I'm afraid.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: You cannot hear me well?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Now it's better.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. AG, because that's how I will call you, I will not use your own name, Mr. AG, before giving testimony in this court, the Rules of Procedure and Evidence require you to make a solemn declaration that you'll speak the whole truth and nothing but the truth. The text of this declaration will be handed out to you now by the usher, and may I invite you to make that declaration.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I solemnly declare that I will speak the truth, the whole truth, and nothing but the truth.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Would you please be seated.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. AG, you'll first be examined by counsel for the Prosecution, then by counsel for the Defence, and if the Judges have any additional questions, they will put them to you as well. Mr. Ierace, please proceed.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I apologise, but I can't hear the interpretation properly.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could we perhaps just test whether you can hear it better now?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It's better now, yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Ierace, please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Good morning, Witness.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AG
utterances.text: Good morning.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Mr. President, I would ask that the witness be shown Exhibit P3677.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Would you confirm that the details on the piece of paper in front of you are correct as to your name and date of birth.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AG
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Thank you. Sir, in 1992, were you living in Sarajevo?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AG
utterances.text: Until April.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: At some stage after that, did you leave Bosnia for a period of time?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AG
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: At some stage in 1994, did you return to Sarajevo?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AG
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: At some stage after your return, were you wounded?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AG
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: When were you wounded?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AG
utterances.text: On the 22nd of July, 1994.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: How old were you then?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AG
utterances.text: Thirteen.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Where were you when you were wounded?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AG
utterances.text: With my mother and sister. I was going to visit relatives.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Whereabouts were you at the time that you were actually wounded?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AG
utterances.text: This was halfway there, I think, as we were going to see those relatives.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Were you inside a building or somewhere in the open?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AG
utterances.text: In the open.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Were you standing still or walking or what?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AG
utterances.text: I was riding a bicycle. During the actual wounding, I was holding the bicycle. I wasn't on the bicycle. I had got off the bicycle.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Please try to avoid referring to your family by their names, but what were your mother and sister doing at the moment that you were wounded?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AG
utterances.text: They stopped next to a shop window to look at the shoes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Can you tell us what happened next?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AG
utterances.text: Briefly, for a while I was riding the bike, and then I stopped next to them and got off the bike.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Please go on.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AG
utterances.text: After I don't know how much time, when I stopped next to this window, I was wounded.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: What part of your body was wounded?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AG
utterances.text: My stomach.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Was that towards the middle of your body or to one side or to both sides?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AG
utterances.text: The lower part of my stomach. I had an entry and an exit wound.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: At the time that you were wounded --

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AG
utterances.text: I don't know for sure, but I know it was in the afternoon.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: What was the weather like at that time that you were wounded?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AG
utterances.text: I'm not sure, but I know that it wasn't raining. The skies were clear.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Are you able to say what it was that wounded you?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AG
utterances.text: I didn't get the interpretation.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: What was it that caused the wound to your body?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AG
utterances.text: Somebody shot at me.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Did you hear the sound of the shot apparently being fired?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AG
utterances.text: This happened in a very short space of time so that I don't remember whether I heard it. I'm not sure.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Did you hear any sound at about the time that you were shot?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AG
utterances.text: I'm not sure.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Did you say anything at the time you were shot, as best you recollect?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AG
utterances.text: No, no. I'm not sure.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: What happened after you were shot?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AG
utterances.text: I entered the passageway that was next to that shop, and a man came out of a restaurant that was nearby. He took me to his car, and then we went to the emergency service.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Did you hear the sound of any shooting before you were shot, say within about ten minutes before you were shot?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AG
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Did you hear the sound of any shooting after you were shot, that is, between the time you were shot and when you left the area for treatment?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AG
utterances.text: I'm not sure, because I was in a state of shock. So I'm not sure.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: You told us that your mother and your sister were nearby at the time that you were shot. Were there any other people in that area at that time?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AG
utterances.text: There were some children nearby.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: How far away were they from you at that time?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AG
utterances.text: Very close to me.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: How many children?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AG
utterances.text: I'm not sure. Maybe five or six, but I can't be certain. I didn't pay attention to that.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Did you notice what they did, if anything, after you were shot?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AG
utterances.text: No, but they probably ran away.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Did you notice any adults in the vicinity, apart from members of your family?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AG
utterances.text: I'm not sure about that. I didn't pay attention.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: You will now see a video on the screen in front of you. Please watch it carefully.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Mr. President, I ask that the video be played which is, for the transcript, Exhibit P3280WW. Mr. President, before that's played, might that be in closed session, and that will ensure that the names that are on the screen at the moment are not displayed.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, could we please turn into closed session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, we are in open session. Please proceed, Mr. Ierace.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Sir, did you recognise yourself in that video?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AG
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Was that filmed in approximately September of last year?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AG
utterances.text: Yes, but I'm not sure about that.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: We saw in the video that you were asked to point to a number of things. Did you do so truthfully and to the best of your recollection?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AG
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: What were you wearing that day?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AG
utterances.text: I was wearing shorts and a short-sleeved T-shirt.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Did you notice any military equipment nearby at the time that you were shot, such as, for instance, military vehicles?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AG
utterances.text: I'm not sure because I didn't pay attention.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Where were you taken for medical treatment?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AG
utterances.text: The man from the restaurant first took me to his car and then we went to the emergency service, and from the emergency service, we went to the state hospital.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: For how long did you stay in the state hospital?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AG
utterances.text: I think it was three or four days.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: I ask that the witness be shown Exhibit P3279WW. Might that be placed on the ELMO.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: In front of you is a photograph, or at least it's to your right. Do you recognise what appears in that photograph?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AG
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: In particular, can you see where you were at the time that you were shot?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AG
utterances.text: Approximately, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Please point with the metal pointer to that spot.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AG
utterances.text: [Indicates]

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Please take a blue pen and place a cross on that spot.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AG
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Ierace, if you ask the witness again to mark a document, could you please invite the witness to do it in front of him and then replace the photograph on the ELMO, because facial distortion is, especially when the witness moves, not as effective as it should be.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: I will, Mr. President. Mr. President, I'm having some difficulty in seeing the cross, but -- yes, thank you, for zooming in, to the technical section. I'm still having some difficulty seeing it. Perhaps I might have access to the photograph.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Usher. Mr. Usher, could you please give the photograph to counsel.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Earlier, you said that after you were shot --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Piletta-Zanin.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] If Mr. Ierace has problems seeing the cross, we have too, in order for the witness to indicate where exactly he was standing at the time.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Would you please show it to Mr. Piletta-Zanin, Mr. Usher. The Chamber was perfectly able to see it on the screen. Perhaps I should ask the parties as well to bring their glasses, not only the witnesses. No. I see that you both are wearing your glasses. So that's not meant very seriously. Please proceed, Mr. Ierace.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: After you were shot, whereabouts did you go?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AG
utterances.text: To the emergency service, as it was the closest to the spot.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Where exactly did you go once you left the front of the shoe shop? Did you go along the street or somewhere else? Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AG
utterances.text: Into the passageway that can be seen on the photograph.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Is the passageway immediately to the left of where you placed the blue cross?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AG
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: I didn't hear the translation, but I think the witness said yes.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: "Yes."

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: To the left of the passageway one sees an awning. You referred earlier to a man coming out of a restaurant. Can you see where that restaurant was in the photograph?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AG
utterances.text: To the left of the passageway.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Is that in fact the area where we can see on this photograph a white awning with some red writing?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AG
utterances.text: Yes. Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Mr. President, at this stage I wish the witness and the Trial Chamber to see the electronic photograph, which is P3279. The case manager will operate that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. But, Mr. Ierace, before doing that, our order is a bit disturbed this morning, as you might have noticed. Could you give us an indication on how much time you would need for your examination in chief? Keeping in mind that you took one-third of the time for the witness that was cross-examined this morning. And apart from that, you indicated that you would not use a lot of exhibits. So I have some difficulties in guessing how much time you'd still need, and if you'd give me an indication, then I would be better able to schedule the breaks.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Five minutes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Five minutes. I then suggest that we first finish the examination-in-chief and then have a break. So please proceed, and may the electronic photo be shown to the witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Mr. President, I correct what I said earlier as to the exhibit number. It's P3279W.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I assume, Mr. Ierace, there's nothing that would cause us to go into private or closed session on this photograph?

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: No, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Do you see on the screen in front of you some shoes behind some glass?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AG
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: We will now move the photograph slowly to the right. Please stop the photograph. Do you recognise the scene which now appears on the screen in front of you which shows the same shoes in the shop --

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AG
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: -- to the left, and then a very wide road occupying the right half of the photograph? I think you said you do. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AG
utterances.text: [No audible response]

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Do you recognise the street on the screen?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AG
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Is that the view from the area where you were shot?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AG
utterances.text: Approximately, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Having regard to your earlier evidence, do we see in this same view the direction in which you were headed at the time that you were shot?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AG
utterances.text: Precisely. This is the direction in which I was facing.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: We will continue to move the photograph slowly to the right. Please pause.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Do we now see a view of what one could see opposite the shop?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AG
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: We will now attempt to zoom the photograph in on the skyline. All right.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Now, the image at the moment shows two cars in a car park, one red and, to the left, one silver coloured. Behind each of those two cars, in the distance, two high-rise buildings and, between them, a ridge. Is that correct? Is that what appears on the screen in front of you?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AG
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Do you know the name of the area of the ridge between the two high-rise buildings?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AG
utterances.text: I don't know for sure, but I think it's called the Hrasno hill.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: On the video, you showed us the position you were standing in at the instant that you were shot. That position had you side-on to the shoe shop. You've told us that the bullet wounded you in your stomach. Were you able to work out what the entry point of the bullet was? In other words, which part of your body did the bullet first enter?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AG
utterances.text: On the right-hand side.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: It follows from the evidence you have given that the bullet came from the approximate area which was opposite the shop; in other words, what appears on the screen. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AG
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: We will now continue to move the photograph slowly to the right. Please pause there for a moment. We will zoom the photograph back so that we have a wider view.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: I think in the image which is on the screen at the moment we see four high-rise buildings side by side in an area on the other side of the car park. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AG
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Do you know what part of town those four buildings -- withdraw that. Were those four buildings there in July of 1994?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AG
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Do you know the part of town where they are, in other words, the name of that part of town?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AG
utterances.text: Cengic Vila.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: We'll continue to move the photograph slowly to the right. Please pause. Having regard to your earlier evidence, is that the restaurant from which the man came who gave you assistance?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AG
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: For the transcript, we see on the left side of the photograph a road; and from the middle to the right, what appears to be an outdoor cafe area with a large Coca-Cola sign. Please continue to move the image to the right. Please pause.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Do we now see the entrance to the alleyway or passageway by which you left the scene after you were shot?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AG
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: When you were taken for medical treatment, what sort of vehicle was that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AG
utterances.text: I know it was the car of this man who was in the restaurant. I don't know exactly what kind of car it was.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: When you got into the car, was it on the other side of that passageway, that is, through that passageway somewhere behind those buildings?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AG
utterances.text: No. It was at the spot that we saw a moment ago, next to the silver car and the red car in front of the restaurant. That was where the car was parked.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: I take it, therefore, that although you went through this passageway, at some point you made your way back out to the front area in front of the shoe shop and restaurant. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AG
utterances.text: After being wounded, I entered with my mother and sister into the passageway. Then the man came out of the restaurant. His car was parked in front. So we came out of the passageway and reached the car.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: At the time you were shot, did you notice anyone nearby wearing any military uniforms?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AG
utterances.text: I'm not sure about that. I didn't pay any attention.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Mr. President, that completes examination-in-chief. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Ierace. As I indicated before, we'll now have a break for half an hour. Mr. AG, after the break, you'll be examined by counsel for the Defence. But we'll first have a break for half an hour. So we'll resume at 25 minutes past 11.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Ms. Pilipovic, is the Defence ready to cross-examine the witness? Or Mr. Piletta-Zanin?

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Once again I can't hear the interpretation. Oh, yes. Now it's all right. Now it's all right.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Whenever there is any technical problem, please inform us, as you just did. Yes. Please proceed, Mr. Piletta-Zanin.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good afternoon, Witness.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AG
utterances.text: Good morning.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Can you hear me? I'm just checking. Can you hear me and can you hear it clearly?

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: But could the counsel please bring the microphone closer to him.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: I will do my best not to ever mention your name or the name of any members of your family.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Can the counsel please bring the microphone closer? We can barely hear him.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: My first question, please. You've told us about your mother, about your sister, but you did not mention your father. Where was your father at the time of the incident, that is, in July 1994?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AG
utterances.text: I am not quite sure where exactly at that time, whether he was at home or at work.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: You are telling us, Witness, that you're not quite sure whether he was at home or at work. What do you mean? What do you mean when you say "at work"?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AG
utterances.text: At that time, he went to work.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Very well. And who was his employer?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AG
utterances.text: He worked in a school.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: And did that school work at the time?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AG
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Witness, was your father, at sometime between 1992 and 1994, a member of the army?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AG
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: How old was your father at the time of your wounding?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AG
utterances.text: Forty something. I'm not quite sure.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Then why, Witness, wasn't your father called up if he was obviously of a military age?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AG
utterances.text: In the early days of the war, like all the men, he was assigned to posts where neighbourhoods were guarded. I don't know how to put it exactly.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Piletta-Zanin, may I just ask you one thing for my own clarification? You asked about whether the school was functioning or whether schools were functioning. I was listening to the French transcript. Was your question about schools generally spoken or that school?

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Mr. President, you are quite right, because when one says whether the school worked, it means the institution, not necessarily one specific school. It means schools, but I mean just did the school -- did the schooling function. How, I would say, was the army, on march and so on and so forth. So whether the schooling functioned.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues]... in translation it says, "And did that school work at the time?" And it was my understanding from your question that you were asking more generally. Could you please clarify this for the witness so that we are sure about his answer?

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, the Defence appreciates highly that you -- whenever you raise the problem of interpretation.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Witness, when I ask you a question, I ask the question in general. That is, to your knowledge, at the time of the incident, did the school, that is, the schooling system as such, was it -- did it work?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AG
utterances.text: All schools tried to provide instruction. Perhaps not full time. There were classes of ten minutes each, but they, nevertheless, did what they could to keep up the instruction.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Witness, I go back to your previous answer. The question was whether you knew whether he was in the army sometime. You said no. And then you said that in the early days of the war, he stood guard. And when you tell us that he had to stand watch, does that mean with the Territorial Defence?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AG
utterances.text: In the beginning of the war, those would be groups of men in a particular neighbourhood who took care of the neighbourhood, of the houses. At that time, the army of Bosnia-Herzegovina did not exist yet, so those were just men, just neighbours who guarded their houses.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Witness, would they be armed guards?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AG
utterances.text: At that time, there weren't very many weapons around, but they tried somehow to mend and make do. Some people had -- would have some odd weapon in the house, and they tried to manage somehow.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Thank you, Witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] General Galic, I'm afraid, Mr. President, cannot hear. His headphones are not functioning. I believe that General Galic cannot hear the witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could we just...

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. It seems that General Galic cannot hear well what the witness is saying.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Usher, could you please see whether the channel is the right one. Which channel gives the original spoken and the translation into B/C/S?

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Your Honour, as always, there is very bad Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. interference whenever we have distorted sound, distorted witness. All the interpreters have trouble hearing, both the witnesses and the counsel.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [No interpretation]

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Counsel, your microphone, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Witness, will you please count to ten loudly.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AG
utterances.text: One, two, three, four, five, six, seven, eight, nine, ten.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] If I understood well, it seems that it is better, but still the situation is not perfect.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Voice distortion gives some interference which, as far as I understand, cannot be avoided. But when it reaches a point where it cannot be understood any more, although it might cause difficulties now and then, then of course I'd like to be informed so that we can see what we can do about it. General Galic, is it, although not perfect, at this moment sufficient to hear the witness and to understand what he says?

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Could the microphone of the accused be switched on, please.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, I can hear enough. I believe it will be all right now.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: As I said, when you can't hear it any more, please inform us immediately. Yes, thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Piletta-Zanin.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Mr. President. And I will then ask the witness to speak up, because when he does it, then General Galic will be able to hear him directly in his own language.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Witness, I'm resuming my questions. How long did your father remain part of what we call the embryos of the government forces?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AG
utterances.text: I don't understand your question. Could you please repeat it.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: I will do that. For how long was your father still a member of what was the embryonic stage of the army of Sarajevo or of the government forces?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AG
utterances.text: Since in April 1992, I left Sarajevo, I cannot be sure about that. I mean, I was not there. And I'm not able to answer this question.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: And therefore, Witness, you cannot be certain either that your father did not subsequently become a member of the army?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AG
utterances.text: Yes, because I was not in Sarajevo, so that I didn't really know what was the situation in Sarajevo like.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: So on your part, it was just a deduction. Would that be correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AG
utterances.text: Well, telephone connections were cut off. I was receiving no information from Sarajevo so that I cannot answer your question.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: And therefore, you cannot tell me either that he was not in the army because you do not know that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AG
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Thank you for that answer.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Ierace.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: I object on the basis of relevance. That is, this line of questioning as to whether or not his father was in the army at the time that this witness was out of Sarajevo. Indeed, I object on the basis of relevance per se as to whether or not his father was in the army.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Piletta-Zanin.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. Mr. President, simply it is a matter of credibility, because this witness told us that his father was not a member, whereas he evidently does not know it. And this --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Let's just go back. Exactly I'm trying to find the exact lines where his testimony about his father not being in the army is reflected.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: In the English transcript, I think it starts at page 37, line 12.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Where exactly, Mr. Piletta-Zanin, did the witness testify that his father was not a member of the army? I'm just trying to find the exact place. Could you please assist me.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Mr. President. I was listening to the answer in Serbian, and my impression was that the witness answered in the negative. I'll try to find it. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: In English, Mr. President, it's page 33, line 19, that he was first asked the question as to whether his father was in the army.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, indeed. The answer is "no" at 21. And the period was correct for once, from 1992 to 1994, and the answer was no. And now the witness says that he had no way of knowing whether yes or no.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Well, I think he then testified that in the beginning, that his father was part of what you called the embryonic stage of the army, and that he didn't know whether he stayed there. And so he gave further nuance about the activities of his father. So to that extent, I would say that the initial answer has been rectified to some extent. And what happened later when he wasn't there, the witness testified that he wouldn't know that. But I think it's not fair to take the witness back to his initial answer when he rectified, or at least amended, the answer at a later stage, Mr. Piletta-Zanin. So therefore -- and as far as the relevance is concerned, I also was wondering, apart from the issue you just raised, what the relevance was.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Mr. President. The witness, to begin with, did not say that he was -- his father was a member of the Territorial Defence. He did it only later on when he said that he was not in the army when I continued asking him of that. That is the first thing. Secondly, what is there that the Defence suspects that the father of this person was in the army, had a role there and had a weapon that we can ask a number of such questions to bring us to the wounding of the witness on the date in question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, but that's a totally different thing. If you stress the point that the witness couldn't know since he was not there - that's what you asked the witness finally - is that the way to -- that part of the case of the Defence? So I still -- but I now better understand what the -- actually what the case of the Defence is in this respect, and therefore, that is not part of the testimony in examination-in-chief, and if that would be material to the Defence, you should put to the witness what the case of the Defence is, as you know. So therefore, if you do so, you may continue questioning on this, but then you should say what the case of the Defence in this respect is.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well, Mr. President. Then I will ask a question which might clear this up.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Witness, at the time of the incident - and I'm going to be relatively precise - in July 1994, where was, physically, your father?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AG
utterances.text: He was working in a school.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Witness, what was -- where was he physically at the time of the incident in July 1994?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AG
utterances.text: I am not sure.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Witness, since you tell us that you are not sure, is it that you didn't know where your father worked?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AG
utterances.text: I know that he worked in a school, but at that time when I was wounded on that particular day, I don't know. I'm simply not sure where he was then.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Witness, since you are not sure about his exact location, could it be possible that he was also in the street in which you were wounded?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AG
utterances.text: I am not sure.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Witness, if you are not sure, you do not -- you do not discard this hypothesis altogether? You do not say that it is completely unacceptable?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AG
utterances.text: I cannot say whether he was in the street or in the house. I'm simply not sure. I cannot answer you accurately because -- exactly because I do not know.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Very well. If he worked in a school, what was he there? Was he -- in what capacity was he? Was he a janitor? Was he a teacher?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AG
utterances.text: He was a teacher.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Ierace.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Mr. President, I maintain my objection on the basis of relevance. Whether the witness's father was a teacher or a janitor or whatever, he's, in my respectful submission, patently lacking in relevance.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Mr. Piletta-Zanin, could you tell us --

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, I shall be happy to do so, Mr. President, because depending on the freedom of access, we know that some people did not have free access to certain buildings, but a teacher presumably has access to a number of places in a school, obviously, otherwise he wouldn't be going there. So that my next question was related to places which could have been used by other institutions, not only by the school. But every time when I try to do that, I mean, the -- the Prosecution then tells the witness what he should say. And we have already heard very many testimonies, and we know that schools --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. You said the quality of the father was relevant for other aspects which have not been touched upon during examination-in-chief, so would you please then -- and if necessary, we'll take off the headphone of the witness for a while so that you indicate what the case of the Defence is in respect of special places to which teachers would have another type of entrance. Mr. Usher, would you please perhaps take off the headphones, for one second, of the witness. Mr. Ierace.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Mr. President, before Mr. Piletta-Zanin responds to that question, I should add this to the basis of my objection.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: The Prosecution has already called evidence of teachers, and no such proposition has been put to those witnesses. Having regard to Rule 90 and the obligations on the Defence as a result of Rule 90, it follows that at that stage of the case, there was no issue with their evidence, and the opportunity to ask them such questions was not taken. Instead, it's taken through this witness, who at that time was 13, in relation to his father. In other words, it is hearsay evidence that he now seeks to bring out in spite of the fact that he had an opportunity earlier to ask witnesses who were directly employed in the education system. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Before giving a decision, Mr. Piletta-Zanin, could you please indicate to us what the quality of a teacher or whatever other function?

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Mr. President. I shall be very happy to do that. If we take the sum of teachers - and once again I hope that the witness does not understand French and English, but it doesn't matter because it will become obvious - this teacher could be a teacher of physical culture and then no doubt he will have access to the gyms which existed. And we know in other cases that the army used those schools either as canteens or dormitories for their soldiers. And it is therefore very important that whenever a witness can tell us something about a school, that he does so. And the father of this witness, as a teacher, perhaps if he taught physical education, perhaps he had access to large gyms and, therefore, could know where they were, the canteens or the barracks of those soldiers. So to me, it seems a very legitimate question from the point of Defence that he knew where all these facilities where, and also if there were other classrooms which of -- were used for military purposes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. You seek this evidence by way of hearsay of someone who was, at the time when that happened, 13 years old.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Not necessarily. Not necessarily, because it is quite probable that if the schools functioned, if the schools were in working order, then at that time, this witness, who was a student at the time, did go to the school, and it is also quite possible that he accompanied his father to -- to the school and therefore could see himself things that are of interest to the Defence. So it is not necessarily hearsay.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Piletta-Zanin, you --

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] My apologies, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: The objection is denied, but could you please come to the point that you just indicated to us. If you say it might be that his father was such-and-such a teacher, why don't you ask the witness? Could we -- no. If you'd just wait until the witness has his earphones on again. Please proceed, Mr. Piletta-Zanin.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Witness, can you tell us, what were the subjects that your father taught?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AG
utterances.text: Before the war, he taught practical training. I'm not quite sure. I was 13 at the time, and I didn't understand very many things. But as a matter of fact, he trained them in practical exercises.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Right. Did you sometimes go with him to his place of work?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AG
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Do you know if in that school at the time of the war, that is, between 1992 and 1994, whilst you were still in Sarajevo and at the time when you had already returned, were there any military facilities in the school? Did the school house any military institution or something?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AG
utterances.text: I'm not sure.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Witness, when you say, "I'm not sure," what does that mean? Does that mean could you imagine? Could you assume such a possibility?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AG
utterances.text: Once again, I repeat: I was a 13-year-old boy. I didn't really have a grasp of very many things. And I don't know. I just can't answer.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Very well. But now you are not a 13-year-old boy. Did you hear your father talk about the school, say something about that school, Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. which would have to do directly or indirectly with some kind of military activity?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AG
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Are you sure, Witness?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AG
utterances.text: Well, during the war, I didn't attend that school, so I do not know.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Thank you for your answer, Witness. Let me move on to another series of questions.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] And can we have back on the screen the photograph which we had before and which needs to have hidden its lower part. And that was the photograph which was shown and which shows the shop window. Once again, we have to cover. If you'd just let me do that. Thank you. It is the same document, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. It is Exhibit P2792. And which photograph would you like to be shown to the witness? Page 2? The pages are on the top of the --

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [In English] I know that, Mr. President. Thank you very much. I'm trying to obliterate everything. It is page 2. ERN 28...

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We have located the document tendered -- the admitted document. Please proceed, Mr. Piletta-Zanin.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Witness, we will see on the photograph -- do you recognise this photograph?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AG
utterances.text: I do. That is where I was wounded.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Witness -- my image is very poor. I don't know whether the -- whether it can be improved. No. Well, never mind. Witness, you were wounded, and you said a moment ago that you were to the left-hand side of the shop window. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AG
utterances.text: Yes, it is.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Thank you for your answer. Witness, I believe that you said that the bullet which hit this glass pane, the window, which was to the left?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Ierace.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Perhaps my learned colleague could take us to the page and line where the witness said that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Would you please do so.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I will take the necessary time to find it again. But let me rephrase the question. I will rephrase the question so as not to waste time.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Witness, you say you were wounded. Did the bullet, having passed through your body, did it then hit this glass pane?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AG
utterances.text: Yes, it did.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Thank you for your answer. Very well. Witness, this shop window as we see it in this photograph, to the best of your recollection, does it correspond to what there was at the time of the incident?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AG
utterances.text: As far as I can remember, because that was --

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
